subject: Order Form & SOW: implementation window shift + Exhibit A edits
messages:
From: Susan Morris <susan.morris@luma.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form and SOW: Implementation Window & Exhibit A edits

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. Procurement asked me to send a few small edits to the order form and Exhibit A for our implementation schedule. Two specific asks:

- Shift the implementation window from "Q2 start" to a two-week later kickoff (target reasons: internal compliance review + holiday schedule).
- Add an interim burst capacity line for month 1 (we expect a 25% spike during onboarding) and clarify billing/proration for that period.

I've attached our proposed markups (Luma_proposed_markups_20270415.pdf). We prefer to avoid lengthy counters but want to capture the schedule shift and ensure the SOW exhibits map to our integration milestones (Milestones 1–3).

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a short implementation delay and whether billing will be prorated for the burst capacity? If you need legal redlines, please loop them in.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Susan Morris
Head of Technical Programs
Luma Analytics

Attachment: Luma_proposed_markups_20270415.pdf (pdf, 95KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Susan Morris <susan.morris@luma.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form and SOW: Implementation Window & Exhibit A edits

Hi Susan,

Appreciate the clear asks and the marked-up PDF — that's helpful. Short answers:

- Implementation window: we can shift the kickoff by two weeks; we'll preserve the targeted go-live milestones but adjust dates in Exhibit A.
- Burst capacity: we can add a temporary burst line item for month 1 and will prorate billing for the actual token/throughput usage for that month.

I'll route this to Legal for redlines (Jonas + Laura). Marissa (Commercial) and I will draft a clean order form reflecting the schedule and a proposed one-time onboarding credit for the burst usage so we don't have to maintain a complex temporary SKU in the long term.

Can you confirm whether procurement requires specific language around "non-availability credits" or an explicit cancellation penalty tied to the shifted dates?

If not, we'll propose the change and send a redline this week — otherwise we can schedule a 30-minute sync.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Order Form and SOW: Implementation Window & Exhibit A edits

Team — forwarding Luma's markups. Quick ask: can Legal confirm redline stance on the following commercial points? Please annotate the attached draft where you require alternate language.

Key items:
- Implementation window shift by two weeks (no change to acceptance criteria).
- Temporary burst capacity for month 1; billing to be prorated to actual usage.
- One-time onboarding credit vs. temporary SKU (commercial preference: one-time credit).
- SLA: Luma asked informally about "non-availability credits" if we can't meet agreed ramp; suggest we keep standard SLA exceptions but offer a limited credit if we miss onboarding milestones.

Timeframe: would like a legal redline by EOD Friday (16 Apr) so we can send to customer Monday and keep onboarding on track.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form and SOW: Implementation Window & Exhibit A edits

Evelyn —

Thanks for the heads-up. I've reviewed Luma's markups and propose the following redline approach (high level):

1) Implementation window: Accept the two-week shift. We'll add a short clause to the Order Form: "Customer may request a one-time reschedule of the implementation kickoff up to 21 days prior to the originally scheduled start date; Redwood will make reasonable efforts to accommodate without material changes to pricing except where verified third-party or resource availability costs are incurred."

2) Burst capacity/proration: Accept temporary burst for month 1 with clear billing mechanics: "Temporary burst billed based on metered throughput; Redwood will apply a prorated invoice for the partial month based on actual token usage recorded by our billing system. Any disputed usage must be raised within 45 days."

3) Onboarding credit: recommend commercial offer a one-time onboarding credit (not an ongoing SKU). Limit credit to a % of MRR for month 1 and explicitly exclude it from baseline committed capacity calculations.

4) SLA language: do not introduce new "non-availability credits" for onboarding; instead, include a limited, one-time service-level performance credit tied to missed onboarding milestones (max credit amount = one month of baseline committed fees).

5) Misc: add an explicit acceptance criteria table to Exhibit A so dates shift cleanly and acceptance testing remains objective.

I've attached a redlined PDF with inline changes and comments (redlined_orderform_20270416.pdf). If commercial is okay with the % credit cap, legal can finalize wording for DocuSign prep.

Jonas
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlined_orderform_20270416.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

- Billing/proration: Jonas' billing clause is acceptable; add a cross-reference to our billing system timestamp source to avoid disputes.

- DocuSign: legal is good with the revised redline; please confirm the final commercial positions (credit amount) and I'll sign off for execution.
